arxiv-2011-11315.title: End-to-end Silent Speech Recognition with Acoustic Sensing
arxiv-2011-11315.creator: Jian Luo, Jianzong Wang*, Ning Cheng, Guilin Jiang, Jing Xiao
arxiv-2011-11315.description: Abstract Silent speech interfaces (SSI) has been an exciting area of recent interest. In this paper, we present a non-invasive silent speech interface that uses inaudible acoustic signals to capture people’s lip movements when they speak. We exploit the speaker and microphone of the smartphone to emit signals and listen to their reflections, respectively.

arxiv-2201-04239.title: Asymptotic Behaviour of the Modified Likelihood Root
arxiv-2201-04239.creator: Yanbo Tang, Nancy Reid
arxiv-2201-04239.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yanbo Tang, Nancy Reid. We examine the normal approximation of the modified likelihood root, an inferential tool from higher-order asymptotic theory, for the linear exponential and location-scale family. We show that the r ⋆ r^{\star} statistic can be thought of as a location and scale adjustment to the likelihood root r r up to O p ( n − 3 / 2 ) O_{p}(n^{-3/2}) , and more generally r ⋆ r^{\star} can be expressed as a polynomial in r r .

arxiv-2308-06879.title: Towards Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation Utilizing the Wisdom of Crowds in Entropy Minimization
arxiv-2308-06879.creator: Jungsoo Lee1, 2] ∗ {*} Debasmit Das Jaegul Choo Sungha Choi, Qualcomm AI Research KAIST {jungsool, debadas, sunghac}@qti.qualcomm.com {bebeto, jchoo}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2308-06879.description: Abstract Test-time adaptation (TTA) methods, which generally rely on the model’s predictions ( e.g., entropy minimization) to adapt the source pretrained model to the unlabeled target domain, suffer from noisy signals originating from 1) incorrect or 2) open-set predictions. Long-term stable adaptation is hampered by such noisy signals, so training models without such error accumulation is crucial for practical TTA.

arxiv-2402-17573.title: HBF MU-MIMO with Interference-Aware Beam Pair Link Allocation for Beyond-5G mm-Wave Networks
arxiv-2402-17573.creator: Aleksandar Ichkov 1, Alexander Wietfeld 2, Marina Petrova 3 and Ljiljana Simić 1
arxiv-2402-17573.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aleksandar Ichkov 1, Alexander Wietfeld 2, Marina Petrova 3 and Ljiljana Simić 1. Hybrid beamforming (HBF) multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) is a key technology for unlocking the directional millimeter-wave (mm-wave) nature for spatial multiplexing beyond current codebook-based 5G-NR networks. In order to suppress co-scheduled users’ interference, HBF MU-MIMO is predicated on having sufficient radio frequency chains and accurate channel state information (CSI), which can otherwise lead to performance losses due to imperfect interference cancellation.

arxiv-2501-15986.title: A Retrodictive Approach to Quantum State Smoothing
arxiv-2501-15986.creator: Mingxuan Liu, Valerio Scarani, Alexia Auffèves, Kiarn T. Laverick
arxiv-2501-15986.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mingxuan Liu, Valerio Scarani, Alexia Auffèves, Kiarn T. Laverick. Smoothing is a technique for estimating the state of an imperfectly monitored open system by combining both prior and posterior measurement information. In the quantum regime, current approaches to smoothing either give unphysical outcomes, due to the non-commutativity of the measurements at different times, or require assumptions about how the environment is measuring the system, which with current technology is unverifiable.

arxiv-2510-21154.title: Access to Klein Tunneling via Space-Time Modulation
arxiv-2510-21154.creator: Furkan Ok, Amir Bahrami, Christophe Caloz
arxiv-2510-21154.description: Abstract We show that space-time modulation of electromagnetic potentials enables Klein tunneling far below the static threshold. The derived kinematics reveal oblique transitions that can connect opposite-energy continua without requiring their overlap, yielding a velocity-tunable Klein gap where transmission vanishes within a finite velocity window and reemerges beyond.

pmc-12746848.creator: William E. Rosa, Jeffersson Santos, Anita E. Agbeko, Crystal L. Barksdale, Scott Carvajal, Denise Dillard, Ronit Elk, Gail E. pmc-12746848.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). People-centered care (PCC) represents a key paradigm shift in achieving universal health coverage and closing global public health divides. Amid growing global health disparities, shifts in epidemiological disease burden, and evolving sociopolitical contexts that affect healthcare delivery and research initiatives, there is an urgent need for public health scientists to develop community-rooted research strategies that uphold health promotion principles and sustain PCC.
